text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Federal government sets up panel drawn from National Economic Intelligence Committee to investigate allegations that the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) opened overseas accounts.
- Only rubber which is certified by the Rubber Research Institute of Nigeria will be exported, as soon as quality control machinery is put in place.
- The Autonomous Foreign Exchange market on which the central bank sells foreign exchange may have closed for the year.
- Eight major oil marketing companies are facing a financial crisis arising from debts of 10 billion naira owed to them by NNPC subsidiary the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company.
- Atlantic Bank, the proposed replacement for three failed merchant banks in which government holds controlling interests, may take over retail banking activities from the central bank.
- This year's Christmas sales are likely to be low as a result of the gloomy economy.
- Manufacturers association calls for national policy focus on small and medium-sized industries.
- Federal government receives report on crashed aviation development Company Boeing 727.
